newsitem.title: DENMARK: Millennium bug could cost Denmark 20-40 bln DKK.
newsitem.headline: Millennium bug could cost Denmark 20-40 bln DKK.

text.p: The millennium bug could cost Danish computer users between 20 and 40 billion crowns ($6.1 billion) to fix, according to consultants quoted by Denmark's Technology Council, which advises parliament and the government.

The June edition of the council's TeknologiDebat magazine, cited consultant Gorm Oestergaard, as saying that a poll of 111 data managers showed that they had little idea of potential costs and a limited grasp of the problem.

"The majority of those responsible for information technology, both in the private and public sectors, guess what it will cost and what consequences the year 2000 will have and in 80 percent of cases they have not sufficently analysed the extent of the problem," Oestergaard said.

The millennium bug results from older computer systems using two digits to show the year. At the turn of the century, many computers will show 00 for the year and interpret it as 1900, potentially creating havoc.
